facts.fact: The Independent reports that the Uganda Police Force's digital Crime Record Management System replaces a manual system based on moving copies of hard case files, and is used by the records officers at police stations; the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.

The Independent reports, quoting the police ICT directorate's spokesman, that the system was pioneered in Kampala Metropolitan in 2017, stalled when station records officers found it hard to use, has been upgraded and tested in Kampala, is to be tested in upcountry stations next, and will be rolled out only once the Police Advisory Committee accepts it; no count of stations is given, and the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.

The Independent reports that police stations currently have one records officer in charge of case files and that detectives therefore keep the files of the cases they handle, the digital system not yet being rolled out; the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.

The Independent reports that the force's own ICT Directorate upgraded the system on the direction of the Police Advisory Committee, at its ICT Research, Development and Innovation Centre at Kikandwa; the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.
The Independent's report names no budget line or funder for the Crime Record Management System or its upgrade; the article carries no date and is dated here by its published year, 2021.

systems.platform: built and upgraded in-house by the police ICT Directorate
